# Feature Request — Lesson Store as an Open Knowledge Format Bundle

## Request

Store the framework's harvested lessons in the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2, published at
https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md, instead of the
single JSON document `memory/lessons/lessons.store.json` introduced by FC-022.

Today every lesson lives in one framework-private JSON file (schema `framework.memory/lessons.v1`).
Only `runtime/knowledge.py` can read it. It carries no provenance or trust metadata that a third
party would understand, and it cannot be browsed, linked or reviewed as documents. OKF is an open,
vendor-neutral format built for this: a directory of markdown concept documents with YAML
frontmatter, plus reserved `index.md` and `log.md` files.

## Expected outcome

1. **Bundle.** The lesson store becomes an OKF bundle directory under `memory/lessons/`. The
   bundle has one markdown concept document per lesson, a root `index.md` that declares
   `okf_version: "0.2"`, and a `log.md` change log.
2. **Concept documents.** Each lesson document's YAML frontmatter carries the following:
   - non-empty `type`, `title`, `description` and `tags`;
   - `sources` (SPEC §5.1): one entry per run artifact the lesson was harvested from. Each entry
     has a required `resource`;
   - `generated` (§5.2): `{by, at}`, where `by` is an actor of the form `<producer>/<version>`;
   - `verified` (§5.3) where the lesson has been confirmed. An operator approval uses a
     `human:<id>` actor, and a machine confirmation uses a `process:<id>` actor;
   - `status` (§5.4): `draft`, `stable` or `deprecated`, mapped from the governance state
     (`candidate`, `active`, `retired`);
   - `stale_after` (§5.5) where it applies;
   - every other lesson field, kept as a producer extension key so that nothing FC-022 records is
     lost.

   Every timestamp is ISO 8601 with a UTC offset, and every actor follows §7.
3. **Same loop.** These parts read and write the bundle: harvest, governance (approve, retire,
   annotate), recall, effectiveness and the aggregation step. For the same lessons, the rendered
   prompt section (`render_section`) is byte-for-byte unchanged, including the CR-005
   neutralisation. Re-harvesting unchanged evidence leaves the bundle byte-identical.
4. **Conformance check.** The framework's verification tooling gains a deterministic check of the
   bundle against OKF §11, which can also be run standalone. The check confirms three things:
   - every non-reserved `.md` has parseable YAML frontmatter;
   - every frontmatter block has a non-empty `type`;
   - the reserved files follow §8 and §9 when they are present.
5. **Migration.** The 42 existing lessons are migrated into the bundle with their governance
   history intact, and the JSON store is removed.

## Constraints

- No run evidence under `runs/` is edited.
- Only the standard library is used; there is no third-party YAML dependency.
- The bundle stays out of the installed payload and the bundled mirror, as the JSON store did.
- The memory optimiser must not rewrite the bundle.

# Change Request — Lesson Store as an Open Knowledge Format Bundle

## Change class

The change class is `capability-addition`, per the Routing Table in `config/self-hosting-profile.md`.
The framework gains two things it did not have: a new storage contract for lessons (an OKF v0.2
bundle) and a conformance-check capability.

Classification evidence:
- `python .claude/runtime/self_hosting.py classify --path` returns framework-internal (`SR-1`) for
  both `runtime/knowledge.py` and `memory/lessons/lessons.store.json`.
- `python .claude/runtime/self_hosting.py route --intent capability-addition` returns
  `/implement` over `implement-feature` v1.0.0 at `scope-and-acceptance`.

## Surfaces this change is expected to touch

| Surface | Nature of change |
|---|---|
| `runtime/knowledge.py` | Bundle reader and writer, frontmatter serialiser and parser, migration, OKF §11 conformance check, command line |
| `runtime/` (verifier; the carrier is chosen in design) | Standalone deterministic OKF conformance verifier |
| `validation/framework-release-checklist.md` | Possibly an advisory item that runs the conformance verifier |
| `memory/lessons/` | The JSON store is replaced by the bundle: `index.md`, `log.md`, and one concept document per lesson |
| `memory/README.md`, `memory/memory-governance.md`, `memory/memory-resolver.md`, `config/runtime.md` | Describe the bundle |
| `runtime/optimize_memory.py` | Possibly: keep the bundle out of the optimiser |
| `omn_agent/source.py` | The installer exclusion covers the bundle |
| `tests/test_knowledge.py` | Tests for bundle round trip, idempotency, migration and conformance |
| `omn_agent/_bundled_payload/**` | Mirror refreshed with `python tests/test_bundled_payload.py --sync` |

## Not touched

The change does not touch gates, artifact validators, Phase Model tables, agent module text, or run
evidence under `runs/`.

# Business Intent — Lesson Store as an Open Knowledge Format Bundle

## Problem

The framework's lessons hold what it has learned about what goes wrong in runs, and they are
locked in a private JSON schema. Three things follow from that:
- operators cannot read the lessons as documents;
- other tools cannot consume them;
- nothing in the file tells an outside reader who produced a lesson or who confirmed it.

## Intent

Store the framework's learned knowledge in an open, vendor-neutral knowledge format, so that it is
portable and can be reviewed. The change must not lose any governance or behaviour that the
knowledge loop has today.

## Success

- The lesson store is a conformant OKF v0.2 bundle, and a deterministic check proves it.
- Each lesson states, in the format's own terms, where it came from (`sources`, `generated`) and
  how far it can be trusted (`verified`, `status`).
- At dispatch, agents are shown exactly the same lesson text as before.
- No gate, validator, or acceptance rule is weakened, and every verifier stays at its recorded
  baseline.

## Non-goals

- Publishing the bundle outside the repository, or shipping it to installed copies.
- Changing which lessons are harvested, when they become eligible, or how they are ranked.
- Converting any other `memory/` document to OKF.

# Architecture Context — Lesson Store as an Open Knowledge Format Bundle

## The current store

- `runtime/knowledge.py` (FC-022) owns the store through three pieces:
  - `load_store(root)` returns the document `{schema, lessons: [...]}`, or None.
  - `write_store(root, data)` writes canonical bytes atomically, through a temporary file and
    `os.replace`, and only when the bytes differ.
  - `StoreLock` is an exclusive lock file, `memory/lessons/lessons.store.lock`.

  Harvest, governance, recall, effectiveness, the report and the aggregation step all go through
  `load_store` and `write_store`. If their dict interface stays the same, every caller stays
  unchanged.
- A lesson record has a closed field list (`LESSON_FIELDS`):
  - `lesson_id`: `L-` plus 10 hex characters of the fingerprint digest;
  - `fingerprint`, `kind`, `artifact_type`, `check_id`, `check_description`, `check_severity`,
    `gate`, `phases`, `occurrences`, `distinct_runs`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`;
  - `evidence`: run-relative references such as `runs/<run>/events.jsonl#E-0029`;
  - `evidence_state`, `status`, `owner`, `rationale`, `remedy`;
  - `history`: governance actions, each with an actor and a time.

  Timestamps have the form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
- `render_section` builds the bounded, labelled prompt section from lesson records, and
  neutralises every field (CR-005). It must receive the same records as before.

## OKF v0.2 essentials

- **Files.** `index.md` and `log.md` are reserved. Every other `.md` is a concept document.
- **Frontmatter.** It is delimited by `---`, and `type` is the only required key. Consumers must
  preserve unknown keys.
- **Provenance and trust fields:**
  - `sources` entries require `resource`;
  - `generated` requires `by`;
  - `verified` is a list of `{by, at}`, and a bare map counts as one entry;
  - `status` defaults to `stable`;
  - `stale_after` is an absolute instant.
- **Actors** take one of three forms: `<producer>/<version>`, `human:<id>` or `process:<id>`.
- **index.md.** A root `index.md` may carry only one frontmatter key, `okf_version: "0.2"`. Its
  body is `# Heading` sections of `* [Title](url) - desc` entries.
- **log.md.** It starts with `# Title`, followed by `## YYYY-MM-DD` groups, newest first. Entries
  have the form `* **Creation|Update|Deprecation**: ...`.
- **§11 conformance:**
  - every non-reserved `.md` has parseable frontmatter;
  - every frontmatter block has a non-empty `type`;
  - the reserved files follow §8 and §9.

## Constraints from the codebase

- The standard library has no YAML parser. The change needs a deterministic writer, and a parser
  for the subset that the writer emits. The conformance check must parse the frontmatter it judges.
- `omn_agent/source.py` excludes paths by fnmatch on the name of each path part
  (`EXCLUDE_PATTERNS`, today `lessons.store.*`). That pattern does not cover a bundle of `index.md`,
  `log.md` and `L-*.md` files, and generic names such as `index.md` cannot be excluded by name
  alone.
- `runtime/optimize_memory.py` rewrites `memory/*.md` to reduce token cost. It skips three kinds of
  file: denied path segments, denied names, and files that declare themselves generated.
- The memory directory is excluded from the context slice (`memory/*`), so the bundle's documents
  are not slice members.
- Tests in `tests/test_knowledge.py` reference `STORE_REL`, the JSON file name, and the
  `lessons.store.*` exclusion. The backward-compatibility tests compare a dispatch by the 0.9.0
  runtime with a current one.
- `change_proposal_validator.py` F9 validates release checklist items per proposal, and requires
  only the mandatory items. A new mandatory item would therefore invalidate every recorded proposal.

## Authoring rules

- Artifact validators reject the substring of the host vendor name (check `C3.2`), so write paths
  without the dot-directory prefix.
- Never edit `runs/` evidence.
- Edit the framework directory, then run `python tests/test_bundled_payload.py --sync`.

determinism.contract: Identical supplied inputs and an identical context snapshot must produce the same in-scope item set, the same exclusion set, the same acceptance criterion set, the same scope decision set, the same open question set, and the same scope verdict.
determinism.orderingRule: In-scope items are ordered by business priority; ties break toward the order the expectation appeared in the supplied inputs. Exclusions, decisions, and questions follow the order the reasoning stage that produced them declares.
determinism.modelIndependence: No module may reference a specific model, vendor, or agent runtime. Technology names are permitted only when they trace to the supplied inputs or repository context.
